If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n59\t/// 3. treat as regex\n69\t        return false;\n70\t    }\n71\t\n72\t    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n73\t    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n74\t    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n75\t    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n76\t    let mut i = 0;\n77\t\n78\t    while i < chars.len() {\n79\t        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n80\t            // Skip escaped character.\n81\t            i += 2;\n82\t            continue;\n83\t        }\n84\t        if chars[i] == '*' {\n85\t            return true;\n86\t        }\n87\t        i += 1;\n88\t    }\n89\t\n90\t    false\n91\t}\n92\t\n93\t/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n94\t///\n95\t/// Rules:\n96\t/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n97\t/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n98\t/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n99\t/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n100\t/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\n101\tfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n102\t    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n103\t    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n104\t        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n105\t    }\n106\t\n107\t    let mut result = String::new();\n108\t    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n109\t    let mut i = 0;\n110\t\n111\t    while i < chars.len() {\n112\t        match chars[i] {\n113\t            '\\\\' => {\n114\t                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n115\t                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n116\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n117\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n118\t                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n119\t                    i += 2;\n120\t                } else {\n121\t                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n122\t                    result.push('\\\\');\n123\t                    i += 1;\n124\t                }\n125\t            }\n126\t            '*' => {\n127\t                // Check for **.\n128\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n129\t                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n130\t                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n131\t                    i += 2;\n132\t                } else {\n133\t                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n134\t                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n135\t                    i += 1;\n136\t                }\n137\t            }\n138\t            c => {\n139\t                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n140\t                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n141\t                // the glob conversion.\n142\t                result.push(c);\n143\t                i += 1;\n144\t            }\n145\t        }\n146\t    }\n147\t\n148\t    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n149\t    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n150\t}\n151\t\n152\t/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n153\t///\n154\t/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n155\t/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n156\t///\n157\t/// # Arguments\n158\t///\n159\t/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n160\t/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n161\t/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n162\t///\n163\t/// # Returns\n164\t///\n165\t/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n166\t/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n167\t///\n168\t/// # Examples\n169\t///\n170\t/// ```\n171\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n172\t/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n173\t///\n174\t/// let rules = vec![\n175\t///     RoutingRule {\n176\t///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n177\t///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n178\t///     },\n179\t///     RoutingRule {\n180\t///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n181\t///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n182\t///     },\n183\t/// ];\n184\t///\n185\t/// // First rule matches.\n186\t/// assert_eq!(\n187\t///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n188\t///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n189\t/// );\n190\t///\n191\t/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n192\t/// assert_eq!(\n193\t///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n194\t///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n195\t/// );\n196\t/// ```\n197\tpub fn match_adapter(\n198\t    model: &str,\n199\t    rules: &[RoutingRule],\n200\t    default: &str,\n201\t) -> Option<String> {\n202\t    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n203\t    for rule in rules {\n204\t        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n205\t            Ok(compiled) => {\n206\t                if compiled.matches(model) {\n207\t                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n208\t                }\n209\t            }\n210\t            Err(e) => {\n211\t                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n212\t                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n213\t                tracing::warn!(\n214\t                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n215\t                    error = %e,\n216\t                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n217\t                );\n218\t            }\n219\t        }\n220\t    }\n221\t\n222\t    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n223\t    if default.is_empty() {\n224\t        None\n225\t    } else {\n226\t        Some(default.to_string())\n227\t    }\n228\t}\n229\t\n230\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n231\t// Tests\n232\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n233\t\n234\t#[cfg(test)]\n235\tmod tests {\n236\t    use super::*;\n237\t    use Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(c, '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\')\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(\n    model: &str,\n    rules: &[RoutingRule],\n    default: &str,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n//
